participation.context: Stood on the Bankside walk and went in.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: The flag was up. The stairs were thick with wherries. You went on into the yard.

title: Looked from the Bankside walk at the Rose flag

participation.context: Read the bill and stayed by the right-hand post.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Came through the door in the lion's skin. He did not speak to the yard.
participation.name: Edward Alleyn

relations.note: seen across a yard, not spoken with

story.body: You read the title and stayed. The first labour was the man in the skin, larger than the door he used.

relations.note: seen across a yard, not spoken with

title: Stood by the post for Alleyn in a lion's skin

participation.context: Stayed at the post and kept the praise unsaid.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Carried the bigger labour. He spoke no word to the post.
participation.name: Edward Alleyn

relations.note: a pleasure he will not spend in the yard

story.body: You let the yard count. You kept the post. You did not speak the praise.

relations.note: a pleasure he will not spend in the yard

title: Stayed by the post while the yard counted

participation.context: Said he is paid by the share, and took the bridge toward home.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Knew him, asked whether wit pays, and named six pound and the jig.
participation.name: Philip Henslowe

relations.note: civil, and all of it money
relations.quote: Ah. I pay by the play. Six pound, and I never argue the jig.

story.body: You gave him the share as your answer. He gave you the play, and six pound, and the jig he does not argue. You did not spend the afternoon's thought on him.

relations.note: civil, and all of it money
relations.quote: Ah. I pay by the play. Six pound, and I never argue the jig.

title: Told Henslowe the pay is by the share
